text:
Alex: Heads up — proposal: SDK adds opt-in headers for client-side A/B: `x-redwood-variant`, `x-redwood-routing-optin`, and `x-redwood-trace-id`. Purpose: let clients request a consistent variant for a user and attach a trace id so telemetry can join client+server. Thoughts?

Maria: Are we doing client-side bucketing or just honoring server-assigned variant? If clients do bucketing we need a deterministic algo so apps don't diverge.

Alex: Plan is opt-in: SDK can do bucketing when app wants experiments without server support. Deterministic hash = hash(user_id + experiment_id) % 100. Server will verify and can override if policy breached. No heavy crypto/signing initially to keep SDK simple.

Cheng: I prefer minimal surface: `x-redwood-variant` and `x-redwood-optin` are enough. Server should validate and drop headers that violate rollout guards. Also: client headers must never bypass tenant quotas or reserved capacity.

Samira: From console UX perspective we should show client-opted traffic separately from server-routed traffic. Need a toggle per-route: "Honor client headers" so teams can opt into this behavior.

Alex: Example headers we expect apps/SDKs to send:
```http
x-redwood-variant: canary
x-redwood-routing-optin: true
x-redwood-trace-id: rdw-7d4a2b
```

Devex-bot: Note: SDKs already expose a `beforeRequest` hook. Proposal: add an `onRouteDecision` hook that returns headers to attach. Example: 
```js
client.onRouteDecision = (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.user || !ctx.experiment) return null;
  return { "x-redwood-variant": ctx.experiment.variant, "x-redwood-routing-optin": "true" }
}
```

Maria: Server-side guard rules we need: enforce max client-side canary % = min(route_canary_pct, configured_client_max_pct). For instance, if a route's canary is 20% but tenant disallows client routing >5%, server should clamp and emit `server_overrode` event. Also add a latency SLO guard: if model latency > threshold, prevent client opt-in.

Alex: Good point. Telemetry signals to emit: `client_routed`, `client_optin`, `server_overrode`, `client_dropped_by_quota`. Include the `x-redwood-trace-id` in logs so we can join traces end-to-end.

Cheng: Tie-breaker rules: when both client and server provide `x-redwood-variant`, default = server wins, unless route has `client-first` flag. We should document precedence: Server > Client (unless explicit client-first).

Samira: Migration note: SDKs default `x-redwood-routing-optin=false`. Opt-in must be explicit and visible in SDK changelog. Add a UX flow to surface undefined experiments to product teams.

Maria: Test plan: unit test the hash algorithm, integration test where SDK sets headers and router clamps traffic, E2E that validates telemetry events show up in console and that the override reason is visible.

Cheng: I'll add router policy checks and telemetry hooks. Will emit `client_routed` with fields `[route, tenant, variant, trace_id]`.

Alex: I'll draft the SDK PR (hook + docs) and a console flag for "honor client headers". Filing issue #4921 and will link design doc + test plan. If no objections I'll start Monday. :thumbsup: 

Maria: +1. Please include a short security review item for header spoofing and quota bypass.

Samira: I'll start a simple UX mock for the toggle and traffic breakdown view.

Devex-bot: Remind: add an entry to the SDK migration notes and update the changelog.

Alex: Thanks all — I'll post the draft PR link here when ready.
